title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 1st Truth Applying The Principle To The Cosmos

questions.question: What two everyday examples are used to help explain the main idea in this passage?
questions.answer: A meaningful book and a strongly made house.

questions.question: What does a good book show must have happened before it existed?
questions.answer: Someone had to write it.

questions.question: What does a well-made house show must have happened before it existed?
questions.answer: Someone had to build it.

questions.question: After actions like writing and building, what comes next in the chain of meaning?
questions.answer: They point to titles like writer and builder.

questions.question: What do titles like writer and builder point to?
questions.answer: They show skills and qualities related to those jobs.

questions.question: What do those skills and qualities prove?
questions.answer: They prove there is a real person who has them.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can there not be an action without someone doing it?
questions.answer: Because actions do not happen by themselves; they need a doer.

questions.question: What is the same lesson taught about a name?
questions.answer: A name must belong to someone real.

questions.question: What is the same lesson taught about a quality?
questions.answer: A quality must belong to a being that has that quality.

questions.question: What is the same lesson taught about an art or craft?
questions.answer: A craft must come from a craftsman.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the universe by using the example of books and letters?
questions.answer: It says the universe is like many meaningful writings.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the universe by using the example of buildings and palaces?
questions.answer: It says the universe is like many built structures.

questions.question: What do all the beings in the universe do, one by one and all together?
questions.answer: They give witness again and again to their Maker.

questions.question: What main rule is being taught through the examples in this passage?
questions.answer: Made things point to a maker.

questions.question: Why is a deep and beautiful book a strong example for this rule?
questions.answer: Because its order and meaning show careful work from a writer.

questions.question: Why is a solid, well-planned house another strong example?
questions.answer: Because its design shows the work of a builder.

questions.question: What do the actions of writing and building tell us about the people behind them?
questions.answer: They show that real workers must be there behind the actions.

questions.question: What do the names for those workers tell us besides their existence?
questions.answer: They also tell us those workers have fitting abilities and qualities.

questions.question: If there is a skill, what must also be true?
questions.answer: There must be someone who has that skill.

questions.question: How does the passage connect skill and worker in a simple cause-and-effect way?
questions.answer: Skill shows a skilled person, and craft shows a craftsman.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the universe and written things?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to many books and messages.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the universe and built things?
questions.answer: The universe is compared to many structures like homes and palaces.

questions.question: What do the words about “one by one” and “all together” help the reader understand?
questions.answer: Every creature gives proof by itself, and all creatures give even stronger proof together.

questions.question: What big belief is this passage leading the reader to understand?
questions.answer: The universe shows the existence of its Creator.

questions.question: What is the first step in the passage’s reasoning when it talks about a book?
questions.answer: It begins with a work that has beauty and meaning.

questions.question: What does that first step lead to?
questions.answer: It leads to the act that produced it, like writing.

questions.question: After the act, what does the passage say we understand next?
questions.answer: We understand the title of the one who did it, like writer.

questions.question: After the title, what deeper thing do we understand?
questions.answer: We understand the person’s abilities and qualities.

questions.question: After abilities and qualities, what final conclusion is reached?
questions.answer: There must be a real being who has them.

questions.question: How does the house example support the same pattern?
questions.answer: A finished house points to building, then to a builder, then to the builder’s skill.

questions.question: Which four things does the passage say cannot stand alone?
questions.answer: A deed, a name, an attribute, and a craft.

questions.question: Why is that important for understanding the world?
questions.answer: It means the things we see in the world must come from a real source.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the whole universe and everything in it?
questions.answer: It is like a huge collection of meaningful works.

questions.question: What are the two tools used in the comparison about the universe?
questions.answer: A pen for writing and a hammer for building.

questions.question: Do those tools mean ordinary human tools here, or do they help explain a bigger truth?
questions.answer: They help explain a bigger truth about divine making and planning.

questions.question: What overall message do the universe and its beings give?
questions.answer: They all point beyond themselves to the One who made them.

questions.question: If a student sees a carefully written notebook page, what lesson from this passage matches that example?
questions.answer: Careful writing shows there was a writer behind it.

questions.question: If a student sees a neatly built masjid model for a class project, what lesson from this passage matches that example?
questions.answer: Good building shows there was a builder behind it.

questions.question: How does the passage use normal life examples to teach a bigger truth?
questions.answer: It starts with simple things we know and then applies that idea to the whole universe.

questions.question: Why would a random pile of bricks not teach the same lesson as a well-built house?
questions.answer: Because a planned house clearly shows design, order, and purposeful work.

questions.question: Why would random marks not teach the same lesson as a meaningful book?
questions.answer: Because a real book shows order and understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to notice in things that are made well?
questions.answer: We should notice signs of purpose, skill, and a maker.

questions.question: What does it mean that the universe is like many letters and books?
questions.answer: Its creatures carry meanings and signs that can be read.

questions.question: What does it mean that the universe is like many palaces and buildings?
questions.answer: Its parts are arranged with care like things built on purpose.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of all beings together stronger than only one example?
questions.answer: Because many signs joining together make the proof clearer and greater.

questions.question: What faith lesson can a Muslim student take from this passage?
questions.answer: Looking at creation should help us remember and know our Creator.

questions.question: Does the passage present the universe as empty and meaningless or as full of signs?
questions.answer: It presents the universe as full of signs.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful reader conclude after following the passage’s examples?
questions.answer: The created world points to a wise and powerful Maker.

questions.question: What is being compared to a book in this passage?
questions.answer: The universe and the beings in it.

questions.question: What is being compared to houses and palaces in this passage?
questions.answer: The universe and the beings in it.

questions.question: How are the book example and the house example alike?
questions.answer: Both show that a finished work points to the one who made it.

questions.question: How are writing and building alike in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Both are actions that prove a real worker is behind them.

questions.question: How are the names writer and builder alike?
questions.answer: Both are titles that belong to people who do those actions.

questions.question: How are qualities like writing ability and building ability alike?
questions.answer: Both are abilities that must exist in someone real.

questions.question: How are deed, name, attribute, and craft similar in the passage?
questions.answer: None of them can exist by themselves without a real source.

questions.question: In what way is the universe different from just one book or one house in the passage?
questions.answer: It contains countless signs instead of only one sign.

questions.question: What does the passage say about each being by itself?
questions.answer: Each one gives many proofs on its own.

questions.question: What does the passage say about all beings together?
questions.answer: Together they give even more proofs than can be counted.

questions.question: Which gives a stronger witness in the passage: one created thing alone or all created things together?
questions.answer: All created things together give the stronger witness.

questions.question: What central truth is strengthened by all these comparisons?
questions.answer: Creation points to the existence of its Creator.

questions.question: What kind of book is mentioned at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: One that is beautiful and full of deep meaning.

questions.question: What kind of house is mentioned at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: One that is made well and put together properly.

questions.question: Why are these two examples good choices for teaching the passage’s idea?
questions.answer: Because both clearly show planning, skill, and purposeful work.

questions.question: What must come before the title of writer can fit someone?
questions.answer: The act of writing must come from that person.

questions.question: What must come before the title of builder can fit someone?
questions.answer: The act of building must come from that person.

questions.question: What do the titles writer and builder tell us about the people who hold them?
questions.answer: They have the right abilities and qualities for those works.

questions.question: What does the passage say is impossible about actions and doers?
questions.answer: An action cannot exist without someone doing it.

questions.question: What does the passage say is impossible about qualities and the one who has them?
questions.answer: A quality cannot exist without a being who has that quality.

questions.question: What does the passage say is impossible about a craft and a craftsman?
questions.answer: A craft cannot exist without a craftsman.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the universe resemble in terms of meaning and design?
questions.answer: It resembles a huge set of meaningful writings and carefully made structures.

questions.question: What does this comparison suggest about the world around us?
questions.answer: It suggests the world was made with knowledge, power, and purpose.

questions.question: What final role do all beings play according to the end of the passage?
questions.answer: They act like witnesses that point to Allah’s creating and ordering.
